examples.en: I couldn't do my homework because of laziness.
Stop being lazy and get up quickly.

examples.ko: 아침마다 게으름이 저를 이불 속에 붙잡아요.
examples.en: Every morning laziness keeps me in my blanket.
Everyone has a bit of laziness.
I exercise every day to get out of laziness.
On weekends a little laziness is sometimes needed too.

explain: '게으름을 피우다', '게으름을 부리다'처럼 써요. 사람의 성격을 말할 때는 형용사 '게으르다'를 쓰는데, '게을러요'처럼 모양이 바뀌는 르 불규칙이에요.

phrases.example: 저는 아침에 늦게 일어나는 게으른 사람이에요.
phrases.en: I'm a lazy person who gets up late in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격을 말할 때는 명사 '게으름' 대신 형용사 '게으르다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: To describe character, use the adjective '게으르다' instead of the noun.

phrases.en: I've been so lazy lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: '게으르다'는 르 불규칙이라 '게을러요'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '게으르다' is irregular and becomes '게을러요'.

phrases.en: On weekends I laze around at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 쉬거나 일을 미루는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes slacking off or putting things off on purpose.
phrases.en_equiv: to be lazy; to slack off

explain_en: It pairs with '게으름을 피우다' and '게으름을 부리다'. To describe a person use the adjective '게으르다', which is a 르-irregular adjective and becomes '게을러요'.

examples.ko: 겨울잠을 자는 개구리는 땅속에서 봄을 기다려요.
examples.en: Frogs that hibernate wait for spring underground.
Snakes also hibernate when winter comes.

examples.ko: 곰은 겨울잠에 들어가기 전에 많이 먹어요.
examples.en: Bears eat a lot before they go into hibernation.

examples.ko: 겨울잠 자는 동물은 어떤 게 있어요?
examples.en: What kinds of animals hibernate?

examples.ko: 겨울잠에서 깬 곰은 배가 많이 고플 거예요.
examples.en: A bear that has woken from hibernation must be very hungry.

examples.ko: 저도 겨울잠을 자고 싶을 만큼 겨울에는 졸려요.
examples.en: I get so sleepy in winter that I feel like hibernating too.

explain: '겨울잠을 자다'가 기본 표현이에요. 사람이 겨울에 너무 졸리거나 집에만 있을 때 농담으로 '겨울잠 자고 싶다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: Bears hibernate during the winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이 겨울을 보내는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic expression for animals spending the winter asleep.

phrases.en: When spring comes, frogs wake up from hibernation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨울잠이 끝나고 일어나는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes waking up when hibernation ends.

phrases.en: It's so cold that I want to hibernate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 추위나 졸음 때문에 농담처럼 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking remark people make when cold or sleepy.

explain_en: The basic expression is '겨울잠을 자다'. People also joke '겨울잠 자고 싶다' when they feel very sleepy or stay home all winter.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 긴 국경선을 맞대고 있어요.
examples.en: The two countries share a long border.
Villages near the border are quiet.

examples.ko: 국경선을 넘을 때 여권을 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You have to show your passport when crossing the border.
On the map, the border is drawn as a dotted line.
The border runs along the river.
There is a checkpoint at the border.

explain: 그냥 '국경'이라고도 많이 말해요. '국경을 넘다'는 자주 쓰는 표현이고, 지도의 선을 말할 때 '국경선'이 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 기차를 타고 국경을 넘어 다른 나라로 갔어요.
phrases.en: I took a train across the border to another country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국경선'보다 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more often in daily life than 국경선.

phrases.example: 국경선을 따라 걸으면 작은 마을이 나와요.
phrases.en: If you walk along the border line, you reach a small village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선의 모양을 따라 움직일 때 '따라'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 따라 when moving along the line.

phrases.example: 이 강이 두 나라의 국경선이 돼요.
phrases.en: This river forms the border between the two countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강이나 산이 나라를 나누는 경계일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a river or mountain divides countries.

explain_en: People also often just say '국경'. '국경을 넘다' (cross the border) is a common phrase, while '국경선' fits when talking about the line on a map.

en: to be so; to be as such; to be like that

examples.en: I think so too.
It was like that in the past, too.
Everyone has times like that.
It will be the same from now on.
Because that was the situation, nobody objected.
It's always like that during exam season, isn't it?

explain: 말할 때는 '그래요', '그렇다'를 더 많이 써요. '그러하다'는 글이나 격식 있는 말에서 보여요. '그러한'과 '그러해서'는 '그런', '그래서'로 줄여 말하는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: That's not the case for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그렇다'를 부정하는 활용형으로, 어떤 말이 맞지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when something is not the case.

phrases.en: I feel the same way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그렇다'의 해요체로, 일상 대화에서 가장 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form of 그렇다, most common in daily conversation.

phrases.en: There is no such thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그러한'을 줄인 말로, 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 그러한 that describes the noun after it.

explain_en: In everyday speech '그래요' and '그렇다' are more common. 그러하다 shows up in writing and formal speech. '그러한' and '그러해서' are often shortened to '그런' and '그래서' in conversation.

examples.en: I couldn't hide my surprise.
Surprise and joy mixed together at the sudden news.

examples.ko: 아이들은 놀람 반 기쁨 반으로 선물을 열었어요.
examples.en: The children opened the gift half in surprise and half in joy.

examples.ko: 놀람 때문에 한동안 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't speak for a while because of the shock.

examples.ko: 그 소식은 우리에게 큰 놀람을 주었어요.
examples.en: That news gave us a big surprise.
A look of surprise filled his face.

explain: 말할 때는 보통 '놀랐어요'처럼 동사를 쓰고, 명사 '놀람'은 글이나 감정을 설명할 때 나와요. '놀라움'은 감탄이나 대단하다는 느낌이 있고, '놀람'은 깜짝 놀라는 느낌에 더 가까워요. '놀람을 금치 못하다'는 뉴스에서 쓰는 표현이에요.

phrases.en: I felt amazement when I saw the child's drawing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '놀람'보다 대단하다는 감탄의 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compared with 놀람, it carries a feeling of amazement or admiration.

phrases.en: I was very surprised when the door suddenly opened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 명사 '놀람'보다 동사 '놀라다'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, the verb 놀라다 is used more often than the noun 놀람.

phrases.en: My friend looked at me with a surprised face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀란 표정을 설명할 때 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural way to describe a surprised expression.

explain_en: In speech people usually use the verb, as in '놀랐어요', and the noun '놀람' appears in writing or when describing feelings. '놀라움' carries a sense of wonder or admiration, while '놀람' is closer to being startled. '놀람을 금치 못하다' is an expression used in the news.

en: to bring onto the scene; to introduce (a character)

examples.ko: 감독은 영화 마지막에 새 인물을 등장시켰어요.
examples.en: The director brought in a new character at the end of the film.
The writer brings a cute animal into the story.

examples.ko: 무대에 가수를 등장시킬 때 조명을 어둡게 해요.
examples.en: When the singer is brought on stage, they dim the lights.
We're going to feature a famous actor in the ad.
I thought about how to introduce a new character.

examples.ko: 마술사가 상자에서 토끼를 등장시키고 박수를 받았어요.
examples.en: The magician made a rabbit appear from the box and got applause.

explain: '등장하다'는 스스로 나타나는 것이고, '등장시키다'는 사람이 어떤 인물이나 물건을 나오게 할 때 써요. 영화, 드라마, 소설, 광고 이야기에서 주로 들어요. 일상에서 사람을 데려올 때는 '데리고 오다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The director introduced the main character in the first scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 이야기에 중요한 인물을 나오게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a creator makes an important character appear in a story.
phrases.en_equiv: to bring in the main character

phrases.en: The company put a famous actor in its ad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 물건을 광고에 나오게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone or something is made to appear in an ad.

phrases.example: 이 드라마는 나쁜 사람을 등장시키지 않아요.
phrases.en: This drama doesn't have any bad characters in it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 인물을 일부러 넣지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a character is deliberately left out.

explain_en: 등장하다 is when someone appears on their own, while 등장시키다 is when a person makes a character or object appear. You mostly hear it when talking about movies, dramas, novels, and ads. In daily life, for bringing a person along, use 데리고 오다.

examples.en: Oh my goodness, I left my wallet at home.
Good heavens! It's already ten o'clock.
Oh my, good heavens. What is all this?
I cried out, "Good heavens!"
I saw my test score and said, "Oh my goodness."
Oh, good heavens, we're really in trouble.

explain: '세상에', '어머'와 비슷하게 놀랐을 때 해요. 주로 곤란하거나 나쁜 일을 봤을 때 써요.

phrases.en: Oh my, is it raining this much?
phrases.nuance_ko: '맙소사'와 비슷하게 놀랐을 때 해요. 좋은 일이나 나쁜 일에 다 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '맙소사' when surprised, but works for good or bad news.

phrases.en: Oh my, is it already this late?
phrases.nuance_ko: 주로 여자들이 가볍게 놀랄 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light expression of surprise, used more often by women.

phrases.en: Oh no, we're in trouble! I don't have the key.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤란한 일을 말할 때 '큰일 났어요'를 뒤에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '큰일 났어요' after it to say there is a serious problem.

explain_en: Like 세상에 and 어머, it is said when you are shocked. It mostly goes with troublesome or bad events.

en: to be safe; to be intact

examples.en: My whole family is safe.
There was an accident, but luckily I was unharmed.
I heard the news that the child is safe.
Seeing you safe puts my mind at ease.
I'm worried whether he is safe.
I hope the luggage arrives safely.

explain: 사고나 위험 뒤에 사람이 다치지 않고 괜찮을 때 써요. 장소나 상황이 위험하지 않다고 말할 때는 '안전하다'를 써요. '무사히 도착했어요'처럼 부사 '무사히'로도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The plane arrived safely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무사하다'를 부사로 바꾼 말이고 도착, 귀국 같은 말과 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, often used with words like arrive or return.

phrases.en: I hope my friend who is traveling is safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정되는 사람이 괜찮기를 바랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to wish that a person you worry about is safe.

phrases.en: I'm glad everyone is safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 일 뒤에 사람이 괜찮아서 안심할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express relief that people are safe after something dangerous.

explain_en: It is used for a person who came through an accident or danger without harm. To say that a place or situation is not dangerous, use 안전하다. The adverb 무사히 is also common, as in 무사히 도착했어요.

p.n: 안전하다 says the child is now in a safe state, but loses the sense of having come through the accident unharmed.

examples.en: The incident is reported in the news.
The news of the accident was reported in the morning.
What was reported turned out not to be true.
It will be reported in tomorrow's newspaper.
News about the typhoon keeps being reported.

examples.ko: 크게 보도돼서 많은 사람이 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: It was widely reported, so many people found out.

explain: 방송과 신문이 사건을 알릴 때 쓰는 말이에요. 기자나 방송사가 주인이면 '보도하다', 소식이 주인이면 '보도되다'예요. '보도 자료'는 기관이 기자들에게 주는 글이에요.

phrases.en: That story is on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보도되다'를 쉬운 말로 바꾼 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say 보도되다.

phrases.en: The accident was widely reported.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많은 방송과 신문이 다뤘다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means many broadcasts and papers covered it.

phrases.en: That incident hasn't been reported yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 뉴스에 나오지 않았다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form meaning it hasn't appeared in the news yet.

explain_en: Used when the press announces an event. With a reporter or broadcaster as subject it is the active verb; with the news as subject it is this passive. A press release is the related noun phrase.

en: to be dissatisfied; to be discontented

examples.en: My pay is low, so I'm a little dissatisfied.
The customer made a dissatisfied face at the service.

examples.ko: 동생은 방을 치우라고 하면 불만스럽게 대답해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling answers sulkily when told to clean the room.
I was unhappy with the result, but I didn't say anything.

examples.ko: 많이 불만스러우면 참지 말고 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you're very dissatisfied, don't hold it in, please tell me.

examples.ko: 대접이 불만스러워서 그 식당에 다시 안 갔어요.
examples.en: I was unhappy with the treatment, so I didn't go back to that restaurant.

explain: 마음에 안 들어서 속이 불편하고 표정이나 말투에 드러날 때 써요. 말로 직접 따지는 것은 '불평하다'예요. '불만스럽다'는 마음 상태를 말해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling looked at me with a dissatisfied expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불만스럽다'를 '-ㄴ' 꼴로 바꿔 표정이나 얼굴을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective changes to its -ㄴ form to describe a look or face.

phrases.en: I am a bit unhappy with my company these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '불만'을 써서 마음에 안 드는 점이 있다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 불만 to say there is something you are not happy about.

phrases.en: I do not like the color of the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻을 아주 쉽게 말하는 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very easy everyday way to say the same thing.

explain_en: It describes feeling displeased inside, often showing in your face or tone. Complaining out loud is '불평하다'; '불만스럽다' is about the state of mind.

examples.ko: 이 도서관은 책을 빌리면 스탬프를 찍어 줘요.
examples.en: This library stamps your book when you borrow it.

examples.ko: 스탬프가 번져서 글자가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The stamp smudged, so the letters are hard to see.
Collecting stamps in my passport is my hobby.

examples.ko: 카페에서 커피를 사면 스탬프 한 개를 줘요.
examples.en: If you buy coffee at the cafe, they give you one stamp.
The children made a pretty picture with stamps.
After using a stamp, I close the lid.

explain: '도장'과 비슷하지만, 이름을 확인하는 용도는 보통 '도장'이라고 해요. 그림이나 모양이 있는 기념용·장식용은 '스탬프'라고 해요. 카페의 '스탬프 쿠폰'도 이 말이에요.

phrases.en: I got a stamp at every place I visited.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도장 모양을 종이에 누를 때 '찍다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 찍다 for pressing the mark on paper.

phrases.en: This cafe gives out stamp coupons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 모으는 쿠폰 카드를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The coupon card collected at shops.

phrases.example: 스탬프를 열 개 모으면 커피가 무료예요.
phrases.en: If you collect ten stamps, the coffee is free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카드에 도장을 채워 가는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means filling up a card with stamps.

explain_en: It is similar to '도장', but a stamp used to confirm a name is usually called '도장'. A commemorative or decorative stamp with a picture or shape is a '스탬프'. A cafe's '스탬프 쿠폰' uses this word too.

en: to part; to be separated from someone (formal)

examples.en: That couple broke up last month.
I'm so sad because I was separated from my family.

examples.ko: 사랑하는 사람과 이별하는 일은 정말 힘들어요.
examples.en: Parting with someone you love is really hard.
I had to say goodbye to my friend at the airport.
We were together for a long time, but we ended up parting.
Tears came when we parted.

explain: 이별하다는 사랑하는 사람이나 가까운 사람과 헤어지는 거예요. 연인이 헤어질 때는 '헤어지다'를 훨씬 자주 쓰고, 이별하다는 노래 가사나 글에서 더 많이 보여요. 가족이나 오랜 인연과 오래 못 만나게 될 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 서로 사랑했지만 결국 헤어졌어요.
phrases.en: The two loved each other but finally broke up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 이별하다보다 훨씬 자주 쓰는 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more natural word in speech than 이별하다.

phrases.en: Parting is always sad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헤어짐 그 자체를 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun for the act of parting itself.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날에는 이별 노래를 들어요.
phrases.en: I listen to breakup songs on rainy days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이별 이야기를 담은 노래를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for songs about parting or breakups.

explain_en: 이별하다 is parting from someone you love or are close to. For couples, '헤어지다' is used far more in speech; 이별하다 appears more in song lyrics and writing. It also fits parting from family or a long-standing tie when you won't meet for a long time.

examples.en: He cursed the friend who betrayed him.
There is no use in cursing a bad fate.

examples.ko: 아무리 화가 나도 남을 저주하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: No matter how angry you are, you should not curse others.

examples.ko: 그 마녀는 왕자가 개구리가 되라고 저주했어요.
examples.en: The witch cursed the prince, saying he should become a frog.
I wrote a song that curses the world.

examples.ko: 일이 안 풀릴 때 자기 운을 저주한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: There was a time I cursed my own luck when things went wrong.

explain: 이야기에서는 '개구리가 되라고 저주하다'처럼 저주의 내용을 '-라고'로 이어 말하기도 해요. 사람뿐 아니라 '운명', '세상' 같은 것도 저주의 대상이 돼요. '욕하다'보다 훨씬 무거운 말이에요.

phrases.en: Please don't curse others.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저주하다'를 부정 명령형으로 말하는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command form of 저주하다.

phrases.en: People call it a cursed castle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저주를 당한 대상을 꾸밀 때 '저주받은'으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as 저주받은 to describe something that is cursed.

phrases.en: I was angry and said words of cursing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이 생기라고 비는 말을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Words wishing bad things on someone.

explain_en: In stories the content of the curse can follow with '-라고', as in '개구리가 되라고 저주하다' (curse someone to become a frog). Things like fate or the world can be the target too. It is a much heavier word than ordinary swearing.

examples.en: Please take a number ticket first at the reception counter.
I don't know where the reception counter is.

examples.ko: 병원 접수창구 앞에 사람들이 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: People lined up in front of the hospital reception counter.
You can just hand in the documents at the application counter.
The application counter is open until six in the evening.
The staff at the application counter guided me kindly.

explain: 병원, 구청, 학원처럼 신청하거나 서류를 내는 곳의 창구를 말해요. '접수처'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, '창구'는 직원이 앉아 있는 칸막이 자리를 가리키는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: The reception desk is on the first floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '접수창구'와 같은 곳을 가리키지만, 창구 자리보다 접수하는 장소 전체를 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the same place, but it feels like the whole area for registration rather than the staffed window itself.

phrases.en: Take your documents and go to the application counter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류를 내거나 신청하러 갈 때 '에 가다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 'to go' when you head there to submit documents or apply.

phrases.example: 접수창구 앞에 사람들이 길게 줄을 서 있어요.
phrases.en: People are lined up in front of the application counter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 창구 앞에서 기다리거나 줄을 설 때 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when waiting or standing in line at the counter.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the application counter

explain_en: It is the counter at places like hospitals, offices and academies where you apply or hand in documents. '접수처' is used similarly, but '창구' more strongly suggests the partitioned spot where a staff member sits.

examples.en: You have to prepare food with clean hands.
How should I cook this mushroom to make it tasty?
Cook the chicken until it is done all the way through.
A chef prepares the food in the restaurant kitchen.
Eat the food I just cooked right away.

examples.ko: 가스레인지 없이 전기로 조리할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can cook with electricity, without a gas stove.

explain: 집에서 가볍게 말할 때는 '요리하다'나 '만들다'를 더 많이 써요. '조리하다'는 포장지, 식당 위생 안내, 레시피 같은 글에서 자주 보여요. '조리 방법', '조리 시간', '조리법'처럼 앞에 붙여 쓰는 말이 많으니 포장지에서 찾아보세요.

phrases.en: The cooking instructions are on the package.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포장지나 레시피에서 자주 보이는 글말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Written language often seen on packages and recipes.

phrases.en: The cooking time is five minutes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 만드는 데 걸리는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The time it takes to prepare the food.

phrases.en: I cook at home on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 가볍게 말할 때는 '조리하다'보다 이 말을 더 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In casual talk at home, this is used more than 조리하다.

explain_en: In casual home talk people use '요리하다' or '만들다' more. 조리하다 shows up in packaging, restaurant hygiene notices, and recipes. It often forms phrases like '조리 방법' (cooking method), '조리 시간' (cooking time), and '조리법' (recipe), so look for them on food packages.

examples.en: I hear a bell ringing from far away.
I took a walk listening to the church bell.
I woke up startled by the sound of a bell.
The school bell is a signal that class is over.
On New Year's we make wishes along with the sound of the bell.
It is a quiet village where not even a bell can be heard.

explain: '종소리가 울리다', '종소리가 들리다'처럼 써요. 종은 '치다'나 '울리다'와 함께 써서 '종을 치다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: When the new year comes, people ring the bell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종소리를 내려고 종을 두드리는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The action of striking a bell to make the sound.

phrases.en: A bell rings every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 퍼져 나가는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the sound spreading out.

phrases.en: The bell was so loud that I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리의 크기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about how loud the sound is.

explain_en: It goes with '종소리가 울리다' and '종소리가 들리다'. The bell itself pairs with '치다' or '울리다', as in '종을 치다'.

examples.en: I got the date wrong and came early.
I mistook someone else for my friend.
I think I got something mixed up.
I set an alarm so I wouldn't mix up the time.
I mistakenly thought it was Monday and went to school.

examples.ko: 자기가 제일 잘한다고 착각하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people delude themselves into thinking they're the best.

explain: 'A를 B로 착각하다'처럼 다른 것을 같은 것으로 잘못 생각할 때 써요. '오해하다'는 상대 말이나 행동의 뜻을 잘못 받아들이는 것이라서 다르게 써요. 명사 '착각'은 '착각이에요', '착각에 빠지다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Please don't mistake me for someone else.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 잘못 생각하지 않게 말할 때 쓰는 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A command form for telling someone not to get the wrong idea.

phrases.en: That's just my mistake; I was wrong about it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '착각'으로 잘못 생각한 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 착각 to say that one's thinking was wrong.

phrases.example: 그는 자기가 제일 잘한다는 착각에 빠졌어요.
phrases.en: He fell under the illusion that he is the best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못된 생각을 사실이라고 믿을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone believes a wrong idea is true.

explain_en: It is used in 'A를 B로 착각하다' when you wrongly take one thing for another. 오해하다 means misreading what someone said or did, so it is used differently. The noun 착각 appears in 착각이에요 and 착각에 빠지다.

en: to be destructed; to be destroyed; to be devastated

examples.en: Many buildings were destroyed by the earthquake.

examples.ko: 숲이 파괴되면 동물들이 살 곳을 잃어요.
examples.en: If the forest is destroyed, animals lose their homes.

examples.ko: 오래된 다리가 완전히 파괴돼서 길이 막혔어요.
examples.en: The old bridge was completely destroyed, so the road was blocked.
The speed at which the environment is being destroyed is too fast.

examples.ko: 파괴된 마을을 다시 짓는 데 몇 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took years to rebuild the destroyed village.

examples.ko: 이 오래된 성벽은 큰 홍수에 쉽게 파괴될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This old wall can easily be destroyed in a big flood.

explain: 무겁고 강한 말이라 건물, 자연, 환경처럼 큰 대상이 크게 망가질 때 써요. 컵이나 휴대폰이 고장 났다면 '부서지다', '망가지다'가 자연스러워요. 마음이 크게 흔들릴 때는 '무너지다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The village was completely destroyed by the war.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완전히'를 넣어 크게 망가진 정도를 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 완전히 stresses the extent of the damage.

phrases.en: If there is a lot of garbage, the environment is destroyed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자연이나 환경 이야기에서 가장 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Appears most often in talk about nature and the environment.

phrases.en: They rebuilt the destroyed building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰는 형태로, 이미 망가진 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun for something already ruined.

explain_en: This is a heavy, strong word for large things being badly wrecked, such as buildings, nature, or the environment. For a broken cup or phone, 부서지다 or 망가지다 is natural. When someone's heart collapses, use 무너지다.
